entry.title: Application by Mrs Allison Hawking [2026] FWC 2716
entry.content:
Ms Hawking applied for a stop-bullying order claiming her General Manager bullied her by reducing her night shifts, allegedly 'banning' her from picking up extra shifts, and mishandling her complaints after she gave a witness statement about a coworker's injury. Deputy President Bell found there was no ban, no punishment, and no repeated unreasonable behaviour, characterising the hours dispute and workload complaints as ordinary workplace events rather than bullying.

Fair Work Commission, 20 Jul 2026, [2026] FWC 2716

Full text on AustLII. Not legal advice; the full text on AustLII is the authoritative version.

entry.title: Application by CFMEU (105N) [2026] FWC 2224
entry.content:
The CFMEU applied under s 229 of the Fair Work Act for a bargaining order concerning proposed enterprise agreement bargaining with Onslow Salt for Production and Maintenance employees at its salt mine in Onslow, WA. The central issue was whether the CFMEU was entitled under its eligibility rules to represent those employees.

entry.title: Application by Adriana Turk [2025] FWC 3893
entry.content:
A volunteer wildlife carer applied for a stop-bullying order against WIRES, a not-for-profit wildlife rescue organisation. WIRES objected on the basis that it is not a constitutionally-covered business (not a trading or financial corporation), so the Commission lacked jurisdiction.

Fair Work Commission, 21 Dec 2025, [2025] FWC 3893

Full text on AustLII. Not legal advice; the full text on AustLII is the authoritative version.

entry.title: Application by Mr Andrew Little [2025] FWC 3401
entry.content:
Mr Little applied under s.789FC for orders to stop bullying, alleging that Alpine Resorts Victoria failed to provide him the tools to perform his volunteer ski patroller role and blocked him from working the 2025 season. The Commission found that the alleged behaviour did not occur while he was at work in ARV's business, as he had not carried out any work for ARV since 2024. The application was dismissed for want of jurisdiction under s.789FD.

Fair Work Commission, 14 Nov 2025, [2025] FWC 3401

Full text on AustLII. Not legal advice; the full text on AustLII is the authoritative version.

entry.title: Application by Mr Wang Lu [2025] FWC 3129
entry.content:
Mr Lu, a McDonald's crew member, applied for stop bullying orders against the business owner and his manager alleging psychological bullying and coercion during meetings. The Commission found the alleged conduct was reasonable management action carried out in a reasonable manner and that Mr Lu had unreasonable expectations, and since he had no plans to return to work there was no future risk of bullying.

Fair Work Commission, 17 Oct 2025, [2025] FWC 3129

entry.title: Application by Mrs Seema Kurup [2025] FWC 921
entry.content:
Mrs Seema Kurup applied under s.789FC of the Fair Work Act 2009 for an order to stop bullying, alleging that her managers Deanne Scholfield and Janet Stoffels bullied her during a performance review and related processes. The Commission examined the alleged conduct in detail, found shortcomings in how the employer handled the performance review and internal investigation, and ultimately did not make a stop bullying order but provided extensive recommendations to the employer to improve its processes and address the workplace dynamics.

Fair Work Commission, 22 Aug 2025, [2025] FWC 921

Full text on AustLII. Not legal advice; the full text on AustLII is the authoritative version.

entry.title: Application by Mr Joseph Osure [2025] FWC 1346
entry.content:
Mr Osure applied for a stop bullying order against the NDIA and two co-workers, alleging bullying since August 2024. The Commission found that a restructure had removed the co-workers' managerial responsibility over Mr Osure and that he would not work in physical proximity to them, so there was no risk he would continue to be bullied at work. The application was dismissed for want of jurisdiction.

Fair Work Commission, 14 May 2025, [2025] FWC 1346
